fixes.explanation: Yes, Herod, friend. Manaen had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch (Acts 13:1). He's listed right there with the prophets and teachers at Antioch. I think that's quite a background for one teacher.

Philip is a fair try, but the text doesn't say that here. Acts 13:1 says Manaen had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch. A tetrarch was a ruler over one part of a region. Philip isn't named in this verse.

Simeon called Niger and Lucius of Cyrene are both on the list, friend, so you were close to the right list. But the Holy Spirit says, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.” (Acts 13:2) Barnabas and Saul are the two named right there in the verse.

Lucius of Cyrene and Manaen are both listed with the prophets and teachers, but the Spirit didn't name them for this work. He says, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.” (Acts 13:2) Barnabas and Saul are the two.

Yes, friend. After they had fasted and prayed, they laid their hands on them and sent them off (Acts 13:3). Hands laid on Barnabas and Saul, and then off they went. I bet those two remembered that moment.

Letters would've been handy on a trip like this, but Acts 13:3 doesn't mention any. It says they fasted and prayed, laid their hands on Barnabas and Saul, and sent them off. That's the whole sendoff. I'd have packed a box of cookies, but that's me.
Crete is an island too, so your instinct was sound. But Acts 13:4 says they sailed from Seleucia to Cyprus. Crete isn't in this passage.
Malta is an island, friend, but it's not the one in this verse. Acts 13:4 says they sailed from Seleucia to Cyprus. Malta isn't in this passage at all.
That would be a rude way to greet guests, friend. But Acts 13:7 says the proconsul summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God. He called them in to listen.

That's it. Elymas opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul from the faith (Acts 13:8). Remember the proconsul is the one who summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God (Acts 13:7). Elymas is the one who opposed them.

Running is a fair guess, but that's not what the verse says. Acts 13:11 says mist and darkness came over him, and he groped about, seeking someone to lead him by the hand. He's reaching out, not bolting.
